sources.title: Vadym Kliuchnikov, Dmitri Maslov, and Michele Mosca, Practical approximation of single-qubit unitaries by single-qubit quantum circuits, arXiv:1206.5236
sources.locator: Complete 23-page paper; inspected §§2–5 and Appendices A–B. Exact synthesis and gate conventions: §§2–4; denominator and finite descent: Definitions1–2, Lemmas2–5, Algorithm1, §5 and Algorithm2; unit-circle statement: AppendixA; H/T optimality: AppendixB.

contents.name: Theorem1: one-qubit H/T exactness iff entries lie in Z[1/sqrt(2),i]
contents.support: The local statement uses the equivalent ring Z[omega,1/2]. Its converse is proved here through the local state-preparation/descent supplier; no multi-qubit analogue is asserted.

contents.name: Definitions1–2 and the squared-entry sde convention, including threshold3
contents.support: The local denominator definition uses the source base sqrt(2), permits negative exponents, treats zero separately, and measures sde(|U_00|^2), not sde(U_00).

contents.name: Lemmas2–5: denominator change, unit-state equal exponents, and exact descent alternatives
contents.support: The local proof reproduces the algebraic inequalities and independently checks the finite modulo-8 residue search; the paper’s computer-search assertion is not used alone.

contents.name: AppendixA: unit-modulus elements of Z[1/sqrt(2),i] are eighth roots of unity
contents.support: The local proof uses the paper’s coefficient/valuation route with a separately proved sqrt(2)-divisibility criterion; it does not import an unproved ideal-factorization step.

contents.name: Section3 normal form and determinant phase of a two-by-two ring unitary
contents.support: The local statement spells out the exact matrix [[u,-omega^j conjugate(v)],[v,omega^j conjugate(u)]] and proves it from the first column and determinant.

contents.name: Algorithm1 and AppendixB H/T-count theorem
contents.support: The local procedure specifies exact coefficient tests, descent and a certified base table. AppendixB’s omitted finite table and case details are treated as local authoring obligations, not covered by the source citation.

contents.name: Section2 controlled-T determinant obstruction and Figure1 clean-ancilla circuit
contents.support: The determinant argument is fully derived locally. Figure1 motivates a three-wire clean-ancilla construction; the exact Toffoli word and all eight basis actions are checked locally.

contents.name: A finite Clifford+T period and an exact-gate limitation example
contents.support: T^8=I and the selected Rz(pi/16) ring obstruction are verified locally; the paper does not supply this exact pair of example claims as a worked proof.

contents.name: The paper’s historical multi-qubit ring criterion conjecture
contents.reason: No multi-qubit exact ring characterization is asserted. The controlled-T counterexample distinguishes two-wire ancilla-free impossibility from a three-wire clean-ancilla construction.

contents.name: The exact dyadic cyclotomic ring and canonical coefficient representation
contents.support: KMM identifies the exact H/T entry ring. The local carrier fixes its eighth-cyclotomic presentation and proves the coefficient and dyadic-denominator encoding separately.

contents.name: Power-basis coefficient encoding and square-root-of-two divisibility tests
contents.support: The paper uses the same ring convention. Existence, uniqueness, and the divisibility criterion are proved locally from the published cyclotomic integral-basis interface.

contents.name: Squared-entry denominator identity and its nonzero boundary
contents.support: The paper uses the squared-modulus denominator exponent. The local proof states the zero case separately and derives the two possible valuation corrections.

contents.name: Denominator exponent set is nonempty and bounded below
contents.support: The source gives the denominator convention; the local carrier supplies the lower-bound proof needed to make the minimum well-defined, including negative exponents.

contents.name: Exact one-qubit circuit entries remain in the cyclotomic ring
contents.support: The exact gate matrices and matrix-product closure are used. The local proof checks the full ordered-wire embeddings and finite product directly.

contents.name: Determinants of exact H/T matrix words
contents.support: The local proof computes the determinant of every displayed generator and multiplies the phases; no determinant conclusion is left to citation.

contents.name: The finite clean-ancilla controlled-T circuit
contents.support: KMM Figure 1 gives the circuit route. The local carrier expands the complete 15-gate block and its clean-ancilla use without treating the figure as a proof.

contents.name: Exact clean-ancilla controlled-T correctness
contents.support: The source circuit is checked locally on all eight three-wire basis states, then extended linearly to finite reference registers with the clean wire returned.

contents.name: Exact compiler factorization and chronological word correctness
contents.support: The source descent route is completed by a local coefficient-certified base table; the local theorem verifies matrix factor order against the current circuit semantics.

sources.reading_verification: The retained full 23-page paper was read for the exact ring theorem, normal form, denominator and unit-circle arguments, controlled-T section, Algorithm 1, and Appendices A–B. Appendix B leaves finite base and several normal-form cases as local proof obligations; the local table and matrix checks are supplied in this batch.

sources.title: Neil J. Ross and Peter Selinger, Optimal ancilla-free Clifford+T approximation of z-rotations, arXiv:1403.2975
sources.locator: Complete 40-page paper; inspected §§5.1–5.7, §6, §§7.1–8.4, §9 and Appendices C–E. Scaled-grid enumeration: Proposition5.22; norm equation: Theorem6.2 and AppendixC; algorithm/cost: Algorithm7.6, Propositions8.1, 8.2, 8.8, 8.11, Hypothesis8.3; phase: Lemmas9.2–9.3, Corollary9.5, Proposition9.10.

contents.name: Definition7.1: on-the-nose operator-norm Rz approximation and ancilla-free T-count objective
contents.support: The local definition distinguishes the exact representative and operator-norm objective from the separate up-to-phase variant, and records the input-encoding limitation.

contents.name: Sections5.1–5.7 and Proposition5.22: finite scaled-grid enumeration ordered by least denominator exponent
contents.support: The carrier fixes the exact embeddings and finite coefficient bounds. Any use of the paper’s faster grid operators requires its complete local construction proof; no runtime is inferred from the citation alone.

contents.name: Theorem6.2 and AppendixC: factorization-based solution of t†t=xi, including zero and unit cases
contents.support: The source supplies a full local proof route, but its Euclidean-domain, prime-splitting, unit and congruence algorithms are substantial local authoring obligations. No completed norm-equation proof or acceptance is asserted.

contents.name: Algorithm7.6 and Proposition8.1: candidate-to-unitary correctness
contents.support: The exact epsilon-region inequality and t†t+u†u=1 identity are fully checked locally; factorization, exact real comparisons and termination assumptions remain separate.

contents.name: Proposition8.2: factoring-oracle T-count optimality; Proposition8.8 and Hypothesis8.3: conditional near-optimal count
contents.support: The carrier preserves absolute optimality only under a verified successful-search/solver route and keeps the no-factoring bound conditional on the source primality-independence hypothesis.

contents.name: Proposition8.11 and the paper’s arithmetic-runtime analysis
contents.support: Arithmetic-time statements are retained only with the source’s factors, ideal comparisons, and completeness assumptions; no Cauchy-name bit-time or unconditional Turing runtime is inferred.

contents.name: Lemma9.3 and Corollary9.5: only phases 1 and exp(i*pi/8) are needed for the Clifford+T Rz problem
contents.support: The local proof derives the determinant/discrete-phase reduction and records the separate relative-phase restoration needed under control.

contents.name: Conjecture8.10 and experimental typical-angle observations
contents.reason: No unproved angle-distribution conjecture or experimental count is promoted to a theorem.

contents.name: The cyclotomic real-conjugation embedding and norm arithmetic
contents.support: Ross–Selinger uses the nontrivial real embedding of the eighth cyclotomic field. The local definition gives its Galois action and verifies its behavior on the localized ring.

contents.name: Conjugate norms lie in the real dyadic subring
contents.support: The local proof expands the conjugate norm in the eighth-cyclotomic power basis and gives its exact integer coefficient formula.

contents.name: Exact operator-norm epsilon region for determinant-one Rz candidates
contents.support: The source uses the same Rz norm objective; the local proof derives the equivalence by diagonalizing the SU(2) error matrix and evaluating its operator norm.

contents.name: Rz algorithm correctness when the exact norm and compiler calls return
contents.support: The source algorithm is checked locally from the epsilon-region lemma, exact norm equation, unitary conjugation by T, and exact compiler theorem. Termination remains conditional on the stated solver and exact-real comparison contracts.

sources.reading_verification: The retained full 40-page paper was read for the scaled-grid construction, norm equation, Algorithm 7.6, Propositions 8.1–8.11, Hypothesis 8.3, and §9 phase reduction. The paper does not encode arbitrary real inputs as Turing inputs; the local claims keep that limit explicit.
